title: The Best Homecoming
premise: Tamsin Dravenmoor, the quiet statistician for the Hollow Creek Ravens, has spent three seasons quietly documenting impossible patterns in the team's play — evidence that the town's beloved homecoming tradition is fixed by the booster club. When her best friend Juniper vanishes after confronting the club's president, leaving behind a ring of keys that opens every locked door in the stadium, Tamsin is pulled from the shadows into a dangerous investigation. As the final homecoming game approaches, she must decide whether exposing the truth will destroy the tradition that holds her fractured town together or finally make it worth believing in. In the end, Tamsin finds Juniper alive, exposes the rigging at midfield during the last game, and helps the town rebuild the tradition honestly — discovering that belonging was never something she had to hide to earn.
about_author: Orsen Kavanagh is a former small-town sports reporter who spent six years covering Friday night lights in the Midwest before turning to fiction. They write stories about the kids in the bleachers — the ones who see everything and say nothing until they can't.

chapters.title: The Keys She Left Behind
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. During a routine stats review, Tamsin notices Juniper's car abandoned outside the booster club office, a familiar keyring glinting on the pavement. The police call it a runaway, but Tamsin knows Juniper never goes anywhere without her lucky pen. The chapter ends with Tamsin pocketing the keys, heart pounding, as the stadium lights flicker on for practice. Emotional beat: dread disguised as denial.

chapters.title: What the Numbers Won't Say
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Following the keys door by door — equipment room, press box, a storage cellar beneath the bleachers — Tamsin uncovers Juniper's hidden notebook: game-by-game proof of rigged plays and payments, plus a note naming booster president Dale Merrick. When someone ransacks her locker that night, she realizes she's being watched. Emotional beat: fear hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Friday Night Confessions
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, with a brief interlude from quarterback Eli's perspective. At the pep rally, Tamsin confronts Eli, whose father sits on the booster board, and discovers he's been carrying guilt about thrown plays all season. Together they trace Juniper's last known steps to Merrick's lake house, where they find signs she was held there — and a threat letter warning Tamsin to stop. Emotional beat: loyalty tested; allies found in unlikely places.

chapters.title: The Last Game of the Season
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. On homecoming night, Tamsin uses the keys to reach the press box, broadcasts the evidence over the stadium speakers, and leads searchers to Juniper, hidden and frightened in the cellar below the stands. Merrick is arrested as the crowd watches; the Ravens lose the game but win something bigger. Tamsin walks home with Juniper under honest lights, no longer hiding. Emotional beat: catharsis and earned belonging.
